name: File sales tax returns (equipment finance company)
summary: A lessor charges sales tax on every lease payment, buyout and equipment sale, at the rate of the province where the equipment sits, and must report and remit it each month: GST/HST to the Canada Revenue Agency, QST to Revenu Quebec and PST or RST to British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba. A sales and commodity tax analyst reconciles the billing tax register to the ledger, checks coding exceptions, compiles input tax credits on equipment bought for lease with their invoice support, calculates bad debt and other adjustments, and drafts each return; the tax manager reviews and approves it, treasury remits on the due date and the analyst files online and books the entries. Differences between billing and the ledger, invoices that lack registration numbers, mixed taxable leases and exempt loans, and authority reviews of large credit claims make the work slow.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian equipment lessor with 55,000 active contracts across all provinces, registered for GST/HST, QST and the B.C., Saskatchewan and Manitoba sales taxes, with a four-person tax team.
baseline.notes: Tax is calculated by the lease system at billing from tax codes set at booking; returns are prepared in spreadsheets from lease system reports and ledger balances and filed through each authority's online service.

trigger: A reporting period ends (monthly for GST/HST, QST and the three provincial taxes) and billing issues the month's tax register; annual information returns and amended returns arise once a year or when an error is found.
end_state: The return is approved, filed and any tax remitted by the due date, the tax accounts are cleared in the ledger, and any authority review is closed.

volume.seasonality: Five monthly returns every month; annual information returns after year end and amended returns after audits or billing reviews add about one a month on average.

evidence.note: Monthly filing applies above $6 million of taxable supplies and B.C. lessors must register; the count of returns follows the organisation file's process map.

Organisation file loaded cost (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Job Bank median $40.87 times 0.9 times 1.35 is about $50; the organisation file uses $48. The two analysts also work billing tax exceptions, property tax assessments and audits.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Document imaging and contract file store
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires

steps.name: Billing closes the month and issues the tax register
steps.description: After the last billing run of the month the lease system produces the month's tax register by province and tax type, and the nightly ledger interface posts tax billed, tax on buyouts, end-of-term purchases and remarketing sales to the tax payable accounts; billing sends the register to tax.
inputs: billing, buyout and asset sale transactions

error.defect_description: Interface lines with a new tax code rejected or posted to a suspense account.

evidence.note: Matches the bill-customers workflow, which ties billed amounts by province to the ledger and sends the tax register at month end (steps s23 and s24); timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Gather the period's sales tax data
steps.description: A sales and commodity tax analyst collects the inputs for the return: the billing tax register for the province or tax, the buyout and end-of-term sale reports from the lease system, remarketing bills of sale with tax, manual invoices, and the ledger balances of the tax payable and receivable accounts.

error.defect_description: A report for the wrong period or province pulled.

evidence.note: Inputs follow the organisation file's triggers (billing, buyouts, end of term, remarketing); the wait reflects analysts finishing month-end and billing exception work first.

steps.name: Reconcile tax billed to the ledger
steps.description: The analyst ties tax billed and collected per the register and sale reports to the movement in the ledger tax accounts for the province, and lists differences such as credit notes coded to the wrong province, interface rejects and manual journal entries.

error.defect_description: A difference netted off without explanation.

control.basis: Tax account reconciliation supporting the return figures, tested by external auditors and tax auditors

evidence.note: Typical reconciliation for a high-volume biller; the 25% rate of unexplained differences is an author estimate.

steps.name: Research differences with billing and accounting
steps.description: The analyst traces each difference to contracts and postings, asks billing why a credit or rebill carried the wrong tax or province and asks lease accounting to correct mis-posted entries, and agrees whether the fix goes in this return or the next.

error.defect_description: A correction made in the ledger but not in the return, or the reverse.

evidence.note: Typical follow-up; the wait for billing and accounting answers is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review tax coding exceptions
steps.description: The analyst checks a sample of the period's contracts with tax changes: equipment moved between provinces, exemption certificates (First Nations, farm or production machinery), buyouts and end-of-term purchases, and casualty settlements, and confirms the tax charged follows the place of supply and exemption rules.

error.defect_description: A move to a new province or an expired exemption not caught.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act place of supply rules (GST/HST Memorandum 3-3-3) and provincial exemption rules

next.condition: annual information return or amended return

evidence.note: Each lease interval is taxed where the equipment's ordinary location is; buyouts at even a nominal price are taxable in B.C.; the branch shares follow five monthly returns plus about one annual or amended return a month.

steps.name: Compile input tax credits on equipment bought for lease
steps.description: For a GST/HST or QST return the analyst extracts the vendor invoices funded in the period for leased equipment, with the tax paid by province, from the funding payables in the lease system and ledger, removes equipment financed by loans (which the customer owns) and adds tax on operating expenses.

error.defect_description: Tax on a loan-financed purchase claimed as a credit.

evidence.note: A lessor pays GST/HST and QST when it buys equipment it leases and claims it back as a credit, while loan customers buy the equipment themselves; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Check invoice support for large credits
steps.description: The analyst opens the imaged vendor invoices behind the largest credits and a sample of the rest and checks that each shows the vendor's GST/HST or QST registration number, the company as purchaser, the tax and a description of the equipment, as the credit rules require.

error.defect_description: A credit kept on an invoice without a valid registration number.

control.basis: Input Tax Credit Information (GST/HST) Regulations and GST/HST Memorandum 8.4: documentary requirements for credits

next.condition: invoices lack a registration number or other required detail

evidence.note: Thresholds and required details from the memorandum; the sample size and the 15% rate of gaps are author estimates.

steps.name: Request corrected invoices from vendors
steps.description: The analyst asks the funding team or the vendor directly for a corrected invoice or the missing registration number, holds the affected credits out of this return and diarises them for a later period within the time limit.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Credits can be claimed up to four years later in most cases, so unsupported credits are deferred rather than lost; vendor response time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate bad debt and other adjustments and draft the return
steps.description: The analyst calculates the tax portion of contracts written off in the period from the write-off report (tax times amount written off divided by total), adds back tax on recoveries, applies the allocation of credits on overhead between taxable leases and exempt loans, and enters the return lines in the workpaper.

error.defect_description: Bad debt adjustment claimed on a contract not yet written off, or a recovery missed.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act bad debt adjustment rules as described in RC4022

evidence.note: Bad debt formula and four-year limit from the guide; the overhead allocation assumes the lessor also makes exempt loans.

steps.name: Calculate provincial sales tax due
steps.description: For a PST or RST return the analyst totals tax charged on lease payments, buyouts and asset sales in that province, deducts tax refunded or credited on credit notes, adds tax the company must self-assess on taxable goods it uses, and works out any collection commission.

error.defect_description: Tax on a buyout or a credit note left out.

control.basis: B.C. Provincial Sales Tax Act, Saskatchewan Provincial Sales Tax Act and Manitoba Retail Sales Tax Act: collection, refunds and self-assessment

evidence.note: Rates of 7% (B.C.), 6% (Saskatchewan) and 7% (Manitoba); B.C. allows PST refunds with lease price credits and requires self-assessment on the next return; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the provincial return workpaper
steps.description: The analyst fills in the province's return form in the workpaper (taxable sales and leases, tax collected, adjustments, self-assessed tax, commission and net tax) and attaches the reconciliation.

error.defect_description: A figure transposed from the calculation.

evidence.note: Collectors must file a return and may keep a prescribed commission; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare an annual information return or amended return
steps.description: The analyst prepares either the annual financial institution GST/HST information return, with income and tax figures by type, or an amended return correcting a prior period error found in a reconciliation, a billing review or an audit, with a schedule of the affected contracts.

error.defect_description: Amendment misses some affected periods.

evidence.note: Financial institutions that are registrants with income over $2 million file GST111; treating the lessor as a financial institution because of its loan income is an author assumption.

steps.name: Tax manager reviews the return and workpapers
steps.description: The tax manager compares the return with the reconciliation and prior months by province, questions large movements in tax collected and credits, checks the support for adjustments and either approves it or returns it with review points.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Tax policy: returns reviewed and approved by the tax manager before filing

evidence.note: Typical preparer and reviewer split in a four-person tax team; the 15% return rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Correct the return for review points
steps.description: The analyst clears the manager's points, corrects figures or support in the workpaper and sends the return back for review.

error.defect_description: A correction made in the return but not the workpaper.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Approve the payment and send it to treasury
steps.description: For a return with tax owing the tax manager signs the payment request with the amount, authority account and due date and sends it to treasury; refund returns and information returns skip the payment.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company signing authority policy: tax payments approved by an authorised signatory

evidence.note: A growing lessor's credits on equipment purchases can exceed tax collected, so some GST/HST and QST periods are refunds; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Treasury releases the remittance on the due date
steps.description: On or just before the due date the treasury and cash analyst includes the remittance in the day's payments through the bank portal to the authority's account, approved in the portal by the treasurer, and confirms it to tax.

error.defect_description: Payment to the wrong account number or period reference.

evidence.note: Remittance is due one month after the period end; payments are timed to the due date to hold cash (manage-daily-cash workflow, step s18).

steps.name: Post the remittance entries and file the workpapers
steps.description: The analyst records the payment or refund receivable, the commission and adjustments in the ledger, checks that the tax accounts for the period clear to zero, and files the return, reconciliation and support for audit.

error.defect_description: Commission or adjustment posted to the wrong account.

next.condition: GST/HST or annual return for CRA

evidence.note: Hand-off to close-the-month, where the sales tax payable true-up is booked (step s11).

steps.name: File the return with the Canada Revenue Agency
steps.description: The analyst keys or uploads the approved figures through the agency's online filing service, submits the return by the due date and saves the confirmation number with the workpapers.

error.defect_description: A line keyed differently from the workpaper.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act: monthly return due one month after the period end, filed electronically by large registrants

next.condition: agency review, often of a large refund or credit claim

evidence.note: Monthly filing for registrants with over $6 million of taxable supplies and the one-month due date are stated in the guide; the 10% review rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: File the return with Revenu Quebec
steps.description: The analyst enters the approved QST figures in Revenu Quebec's online service, submits the return by the due date and saves the confirmation with the workpapers.

error.defect_description: A line keyed differently from the workpaper.

control.basis: Quebec Act respecting the Quebec sales tax: periodic QST returns and remittances

evidence.note: Revenu Quebec pages could not be opened; QST filing periods are assumed to mirror the GST/HST periods.

steps.name: File the provincial PST or RST return
steps.description: The analyst files the approved return through the province's online tax system (British Columbia, Saskatchewan or Manitoba), confirms the payment reference and saves the confirmation with the workpapers.

error.defect_description: A line keyed differently from the workpaper.

control.basis: Provincial sales tax acts: collectors must file returns and remit as prescribed (B.C. Provincial Sales Tax Act s. 186)

evidence.note: The return obligation is stated in the B.C. manual; Saskatchewan and Manitoba are assumed to work the same way.

steps.name: Answer the authority's review or document request
steps.description: The analyst gathers what the authority asks for (vendor invoices behind credits, lease contracts and exemption certificates, the reconciliation), writes a covering explanation and sends it through the online portal, then waits for the reviewer to accept the return or propose a change.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Credits must be supported by records kept six years; review frequency and timing are author estimates.

steps.name: Tax manager agrees the outcome of the review
steps.description: The tax manager reviews the authority's conclusion, accepts it or prepares an objection with the analyst, and has any adjustment booked in the ledger.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Reconciling differences
exceptions.description: Tax per the billing register does not agree with the ledger, usually credit notes or rebills coded to the wrong province or interface rejects; the analyst works it out with billing and accounting.

exceptions.name: Credits lacking invoice support
exceptions.description: Vendor invoices behind credits lack the registration number or other required details; the credits are held and claimed later once corrected invoices arrive.

exceptions.name: Return sent back on review
exceptions.description: The tax manager finds unexplained movements or weak support and returns the draft.

exceptions.name: Annual or amended return
exceptions.description: The annual financial institution information return, or an amended return for an error found in a reconciliation, billing review or audit.

exceptions.name: Authority review
exceptions.description: The authority reviews a return, most often a large GST/HST refund or credit claim, and asks for invoices, contracts or the reconciliation before accepting it.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the end of the reporting period to the return filed and paid (authority reviews excluded from p50)
benchmarks.population: Monthly sales tax filers; derived from the filing deadline

evidence.note: Monthly GST/HST returns are due one month after the period end; returns with tax owing are filed and paid in the last days before the deadline, while refund and information returns go in earlier. p90 includes amended returns and reviews; the split is an author estimate.

benchmarks.value: 1% of the amount owing plus 25% of that per full month late, up to 12 months

pain_points.description: Tax per billing and tax per ledger often differ because credits, rebills and manual entries are coded by hand, so each return starts with a reconciliation and a chase of billing and accounting.

evidence.note: Author estimate consistent with the bill-customers workflow, where adjustments are re-keyed from email.

pain_points.description: Input tax credits on equipment purchases are large and rest on vendor invoices that must carry registration numbers and required details; gaps found late delay credits and invite authority reviews of refund claims.

evidence.note: Documentary requirements and the effect of an invalid registration number.

pain_points.description: Place of supply changes when equipment moves between provinces and exemptions need certificates, so tax codes set at booking drift and errors surface only in sample reviews or audits, sometimes needing amended returns.

evidence.note: Each lease interval is taxed where the equipment ordinarily sits.

pain_points.description: Five separate returns on different online systems each month, prepared in spreadsheets by two analysts who also handle billing tax questions, leave little slack at month end.

evidence.note: Author estimate from the organisation file's staffing.

sources.title: RC4022 General information for GST/HST registrants (revision 25)
sources.supports: Registrants with annual taxable supplies over $6,000,000 are assigned monthly reporting periods; monthly and quarterly filers file and remit no later than one month after the end of the period; bad debt adjustment of A x B / C on a return filed within four years, with recoveries added back; late filing penalty of 1% plus 25% of that per month up to 12 months; up to four years to claim most input tax credits; the $1,500,000 threshold for mandatory electronic filing was removed only for periods from 2024, so larger registrants already filed electronically.

sources.title: GST/HST Memorandum 8.4, Documentary requirements for claiming input tax credits
sources.supports: Input tax credits need supporting documents: for $30 to $150 the supplier's GST/HST registration number and tax disclosed, and for $150 or more also the recipient's name, terms of payment and a description of each supply; an invalid registration number can block the credit; records kept six years.

sources.title: GST/HST Memorandum 3-3-3, Place of supply in a province: tangible personal property
sources.supports: Each lease interval is a separate supply; for leases over three months the supply is made in the province of the property's ordinary location agreed by the parties (or registration province for specified motor vehicles), so the HST or GST rate can change during a lease when equipment moves.

sources.title: Bulletin PST 315, Rentals and leases of goods
sources.supports: Lessors of taxable goods in B.C. must register and charge 7% PST on each lease payment and on an option-to-purchase price even if nominal; lessors are exempt when acquiring goods solely for leasing; PST may be refunded or credited with a refund or credit of the lease price within four years; a registrant self-assesses PST due on its next return. Read from the text copy saved under scratch by earlier work (revision of April 2025; the rules cited were in the September 2021 version it revises).

sources.title: PST Tax Interpretation Manual, Part 8: registration and collection
sources.supports: A lessor that enters into leases in B.C., leases property located in B.C. or delivers property to a lessee in B.C. must be registered (s. 169); collectors must file a tax return (s. 186) and may keep a prescribed allowance (commission) when remitting as required (s. 185).

sources.title: Provincial sales tax
sources.supports: Saskatchewan PST is a six per cent tax on taxable goods and services used in the province, including rented goods; businesses operating in the province must register for a PST number.

sources.title: Retail sales tax
sources.supports: Manitoba retail sales tax applies at a general rate of 7% to the retail sale or rental of most goods, calculated before GST.

sources.title: GST111 Financial Institution GST/HST Annual Information Return
sources.supports: A financial institution that is a GST/HST registrant with total annual income over $2 million must complete the annual information return.

sources.title: Wages for financial auditors and accountants (NOC 11100)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages for accountants: low $24.73, median $40.87, high $72.12 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one return. Five monthly returns (GST/HST, QST, B.C. PST, Saskatchewan PST, Manitoba RST) plus about one annual or amended return a month give the organisation file's six; branch shares at step s05 and the filing steps follow that mix, although the simulator does not carry the return type from one branch to the next.

The lessor's taxable supplies exceed $6 million, so all returns are monthly; QST and provincial filing periods are assumed to match. Revenu Quebec, Saskatchewan and Manitoba filing rules could not be opened and are tier C.

The lessor also makes exempt loans (conditional sales and loans), so it is assumed to be a financial institution for GST/HST purposes that files the annual GST111 and allocates credits on overhead between taxable and exempt supplies; the thresholds that decide this were not verified.
A growing lessor's credits on equipment purchases can exceed tax collected in some months, so about a quarter of returns claim a refund or have no payment; large refund claims attract more reviews.
Treasury releases the remittance in the daily cash process (manage-daily-cash, step s18); its few minutes are shown here and there.
Web search stopped working during research for this workflow; sources were fetched from known addresses and several numbers are tier C estimates.

Staffing: modelled hands-on time is about 8 to 14 hours per return (more for GST/HST, QST and annual returns), about 0.5 FTE for six returns at 130 hours a month; stated FTE (about 0.7) also covers tax coding questions from billing and booking, property tax assessments and audits.

Cycle time: the simulated median of about 22 days sits below the 26-day estimate mainly because refund and information returns skip the wait for the payment due date; tax-owing returns finish within a few days of the deadline.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
